fatal_errors: The proposed FCC/σ microstructure is incorrect for the target alloy, which consists primarily of L12 and B2 lamellae with Cr-rich precipitates and contains no identified σ phase.

The proposed 300–500 °C chloride-solution regime is incompatible with the target's 25–100 °C deionized-water tests and would require an explicitly pressurized system to maintain a liquid aqueous electrolyte.
The predicted outcome is opposite to the target result: the eutectic HEA had substantially lower wear, friction, and tribo-corrosion degradation than the identically tested DS2205 baseline.
The comparison omits the target's rapid 1100 °C thermal-shock conditioning and substitutes a hypothetical single-phase HEA for the actual DS2205 comparator.

The cited evidence concerns different HEA coatings and supports separate σ-strengthening, oxidative wear, and galvanic-corrosion observations; it does not demonstrate galvanically accelerated simultaneous tribo-corrosion in this eutectic alloy or under the proposed conditions.
explanation: The answer presents a generally plausible tribo-corrosion feedback—film rupture, fresh-surface exposure, corrosion, and enhanced wear—and proposes a controlled multiphase-versus-single-phase comparison. It is not a reconstruction of the target study, however. It assigns the wrong phases, electrolyte, temperature range, baseline, and degradation direction. It also misses the central nonmonotonic temperature mechanism: sluggish repair and abrasion at 25 °C, optimal film or tribolayer repair and polishing near 50 °C, and unstable oxide/tribolayer fracture with third-body or oxidative wear at 100 °C. The proposed experiment has some discriminating value, but processing a nominally identical alloy into a single phase would alter hardness, phase morphology, residual stress, and passivation chemistry, so a rate difference would not uniquely establish galvanic coupling. Conversely, absence of a higher aggregate degradation rate would not alone falsify local galvanic activity because strengthening or improved film formation could offset it. Direct phase-resolved potential/current mapping, interrupted-track microscopy, and wear-only, corrosion-only, and combined tests would be needed for a mechanism-specific test.
